title: Sex-specific attenuation of photoreceptor degeneration by reserpine in a rhodopsin P23H rat model of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa
summary: Extends earlier work on the drug reserpine into a rat model of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, finding that female rats respond more strongly — with better rod and cone preservation and distinct gene-expression changes — underscoring sex as a variable in retinal therapy research.

title: Epigenome-metabolism nexus in the retina: implications for aging and disease
summary: A review arguing that the retina's heavy metabolic demands and its epigenome are tightly linked, and that this coupling — disrupted with age — helps explain conditions like age-related macular degeneration and glaucoma, pointing toward lifestyle-based interventions.

title: Selective transcriptomic dysregulation of metabolic pathways in liver and retina by short- and long-term dietary hyperglycemia
summary: Feeding mice a high-glycemic diet altered liver gene expression within a month, while the retina only showed comparable metabolic disruption after a full year — revealing that different tissues adapt to diet-driven blood sugar stress on very different timescales.

title: Network Biology and Medicine to Rescue: Applications for Retinal Disease Mechanisms and Therapy
journal: Advances in Experimental Medicine and Biology
summary: Makes the case for treating inherited retinal diseases as a connected “diseasome” — a network of shared genes, proteins, and pathways — rather than as isolated conditions, arguing this framework could guide gene-agnostic therapies.

title: Reserpine maintains photoreceptor survival in retinal ciliopathy by resolving proteostasis imbalance and ciliogenesis defects
summary: A high-throughput drug screen in patient-derived retinal organoids identified reserpine as a molecule that preserves photoreceptors in a ciliopathy model by correcting an imbalance between autophagy and the cell's protein-disposal machinery.

title: Dietary fish oil enriched in very-long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid reduces cardiometabolic risk factors and improves retinal function
summary: A specialized very-long-chain fatty acid concentrated from fish oil improved cardiometabolic markers and measurable retinal function in mice, acting in part through PPAR signaling — pointing to a possible dietary supplement for eye health.

title: Multiomics analyses reveal early metabolic imbalance and mitochondrial stress in neonatal photoreceptors leading to cell death in Pde6brd1/rd1 mouse model of retinal degeneration
summary: Combined transcriptomics, proteomics, and direct measurements of mitochondrial function in a classic mouse model of inherited blindness to show that metabolic and mitochondrial stress precede — and likely drive — photoreceptor cell death, rather than simply following it.

title: Comparative Genomic Analysis of Mycobacteriaceae Reveals Horizontal Gene Transfer-Mediated Evolution of the CRISPR-Cas System in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex
summary: Comparing 141 mycobacterial genomes traced the CRISPR-Cas defense system in the tuberculosis-causing bacterial complex to a horizontal gene transfer event from an environmental relative, with later genome rearrangements explaining strain-to-strain differences.

title: Aging of the Retina: Molecular and Metabolic Turbulences and Potential Interventions
summary: A review of how metabolism and the epigenome shift together as the retina ages, and what that turbulence means for vision loss — closing with a look at lifestyle changes that might support healthier aging in the eye.

title: Genome-wide profiling identifies DNA methylation signatures of aging in rod photoreceptors associated with alterations in energy metabolism
summary: Genome-wide methylation mapping of aging mouse rod photoreceptors uncovered thousands of age-related changes concentrated in regulatory regions, several of which tie back to declining mitochondrial function — linking DNA methylation directly to metabolic aging in the retina.

title: Loss of endocytosis-associated RabGEF1 causes aberrant morphogenesis and altered autophagy in photoreceptors leading to retinal degeneration
summary: Deleting the trafficking gene Rabgef1 in mice disrupted photoreceptor structure and vision almost immediately, with the affected cells showing signs of stalled autophagy — implicating this endocytic pathway as a new candidate for syndromic retinal disease.

title: Improved retinal organoid differentiation by modulating signaling pathways revealed by comparative transcriptome analyses with development in vivo
summary: Comparing gene activity in lab-grown retinal organoids against real developing retinas pinpointed which signaling steps organoids were missing, and supplementing cultures with DHA and a growth factor produced more mature, functional photoreceptors as a result.

title: Western Indian Rural Gut Microbial Diversity in Extreme Prakriti Endo-Phenotypes Reveals Signature Microbes
summary: Sequencing gut bacteria across a genetically similar rural Indian population found that traditional Ayurvedic constitution types (“Prakriti”) correspond to real, measurable differences in which microbes are enriched — suggesting a biological basis for this personalized-medicine framework.

title: Adipocyte model of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection reveals differential availability of iron to bacilli in the lipid-rich caseous environment
summary: Infecting fat cells with M. tuberculosis in culture showed the bacteria shift to burning host-derived fatty acids and dial down their own iron uptake — a survival strategy shaped by the fat- and iron-rich environment of the lesions tuberculosis forms in the body.

title: Comparative Genomics of Host–Symbiont and Free-Living Oceanobacillus Species
summary: Sequencing a gut-dwelling Oceanobacillus strain and comparing it against free-living relatives identified specific genes — including transporters and signaling components — that distinguish bacteria adapted to living inside a host from those living independently in the environment.

title: Proteogenomics of rare taxonomic phyla: A prospective treasure trove of protein coding genes
summary: A survey arguing that most microbial genome annotation effort has focused on a handful of well-studied bacterial groups, and that applying proteomics-guided gene-finding to the many under-sequenced phyla would likely uncover genes missed by standard computational annotation.

title: Expression profiling of lymph nodes in tuberculosis patients reveal inflammatory milieu at site of infection
summary: Profiling infected lymph nodes from tuberculosis patients found a distinct inflammatory and tissue-damage signature — including a specific immune gene running high — that differs from the lipid-handling changes seen in lung tuberculosis, offering an early molecular picture of this form of the disease.

title: Discovery of rare protein-coding genes in model methylotroph Methylobacterium extorquens AM1
summary: Reanalyzing existing proteomics data for a model methanol-metabolizing bacterium turned up 29 previously unannotated genes and corrected dozens more, including one likely acquired from a distantly related organism.

title: Extensive copy number variations in admixed Indian population of African ancestry: potential involvement in adaptation
summary: An Indian population descended from African ancestors and living in a high-salinity region carries an unusually large number of structural genome variants, some enriched near genes for ion transport — consistent with these variants helping the population adapt to a harsh local environment.

title: Integration host factor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, mIHF, compacts DNA by a bending mechanism
summary: Using atomic force microscopy, this study showed that a tuberculosis-bacterium protein called mIHF packages the bacterial genome by physically bending DNA, playing a role in chromosome organization similar to a well-known E. coli protein despite the two having evolved separately.

title: Crowd Sourcing a New Paradigm for Interactome Driven Drug Target Identification in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
summary: A crowdsourced, community-curated effort mapped over 2,500 protein interactions across the tuberculosis bacterium's genome, using the resulting network to flag candidate drug targets — five of which were later independently confirmed in the lab.
